c.tagline: Lakeside towers and the world in one city

emergency.note: 911 covers all emergencies; 311 handles city services and 211 social services.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Kensington Market: the bohemian open-air market's vintage shops and global food stalls
hood_landmark.The Annex: the Bata Shoe Museum amid leafy streets of Victorian mansions
hood_landmark.Yorkville: Mink Mile luxury shopping near the Royal Ontario Museum
hood_landmark.Distillery District: the cobblestoned Victorian Gooderham & Worts distillery complex
hood_landmark.Queen West: Graffiti Alley's block-long murals and indie boutiques

avoid.reason: No true no-go zones, though the Moss Park area around Sherbourne and Dundas East feels rough after dark.
Keep usual awareness late at night around Yonge-Dundas and on late-night transit, and never leave valuables in parked cars.

hood_desc: Kensington Market is a bohemian, multicultural warren of vintage shops, street food, cafes and murals, ideal for young, budget and eclectic travelers seeking an offbeat vibe.
The Annex is a leafy, intellectual neighborhood near the University of Toronto with Victorian homes, bookish cafes and Bloor Street eats, suited to students and relaxed stays.
Yorkville is Toronto's luxury district of designer boutiques, upscale galleries, fine dining and five-star hotels, perfect for high-end shoppers and affluent visitors.
The Distillery District is a pedestrian-only Victorian industrial precinct of cobblestones, art galleries, boutiques and restaurants, great for couples and a charming historic setting.
Queen West is a hip, trendy strip of independent fashion, art galleries, music venues and nightlife, appealing to creatives and younger travelers wanting a cool scene.

water.note: Tap water is safe and among the most rigorously tested in the world.

transit.pay: Easiest: tap a contactless credit/debit card or phone at any reader - one adult fare (about C$3.30 / US$2.40) covers 2 hours of transfers across subway, streetcars and buses. Or get a PRESTO card (C$6) from station fare machines or Shoppers Drug Mart pharmacies. The same tap works on the UP Express airport train and GO trains.
transit.hours: Subway runs about 6am-1:30am (from 8am Sundays); Blue Night buses and streetcars cover major routes overnight.

transit.m: UP Express to Union Station (25 min)
TTC 900 bus to Kipling station then subway downtown (55 min)
